A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TEGA research, benchmark, and authors. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original knowledge graph query-answering experiments, TEGA comparisons, ablations, and architectural sensitivity studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds rotary positional encoding, alternative transformer architecture, and inference-time results.

M1.justification: TEGA retains the same LogiRPE attention equations, token-type biases, and free-variable pooling component. The additional transformer architectures are experimental comparisons, not revisions to TEGA.

E1.justification: Both versions use FB15k, FB15k-237, and NELL995 with the same 23 seen and 32 unseen query types, syntax-compatible subset, and query-reversion scenarios. The added experiments do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds a rotary-PE transformer comparator. New Appendix H compares encoder-only models with decoder-only models using absolute PE and encoder–decoder models using relative PE. The five specialized KGQA baselines and existing comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 introduces architecture comparisons with specified architecture/PE combinations and an inference-latency evaluation in milliseconds. Existing graph splits, query counts, MRR definitions, and training budgets remain unchanged. The new timing experiment lacks detailed measurement conditions.

E4.justification: New Appendix H tests sensitivity to encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder–decoder architectures, while Appendix I adds an efficiency comparison. Existing syntax, permutation, inductive-bias, component, depth, pooling, and attention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, or reports confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. V2 continues reporting single numerical scores.

E6.justification: V2 substantially expands reported results through RoPE scores, alternative-architecture results, inference timings, and separate seen/unseen-query embedding results replacing Table 5's aggregates. For NELL995, new RoPE all-query ID(K)/OOD(K) scores are 58.4/15.7 versus retained RPE scores of 57.4/15.6. New Table 16 reports TEGA at 52.1 ms and RPE at 44.7 ms. Core TEGA and component-ablation scores in Tables 7–8 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The logical definitions, entailment derivation, distribution-shift formulation, LogiRPE equations, query-graph definition, and MRR formulas are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain the two-shift evaluation framework, comprehensive benchmark, transformer design investigation, and TEGA's improved entailment and generalization. The new contribution list and rewritten abstract and conclusion restate these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 removes the limitation that decoder architectures were untested and adds limitations concerning explicit logic labels, unseen operators, and unverified scalability to large knowledge graphs. It also interprets the new architecture and timing comparisons as supporting RPE encoders and comparable computational efficiency.

D1.justification: The advertised code/data access point changes from an anonymous TEGA host to the named HKUST-KnowComp/TEGA GitHub repository. Existing hardware, training, model configuration, and pooling details are retained; the PDFs do not establish additional implementation details for the new architecture comparisons.

R1.justification: Section 7 expands discussion of LLM reasoning, hypothesis verification, and neural graph databases, adding references such as Parmar et al. (2024), Ren et al. (2023), and Bai et al. (2025). Ontanon et al. (2022) and Yuan et al. (2020) are removed. The central positioning against prior KGQA and parameterized-knowledge reasoning research remains.

P1.justification: V2 rewords the abstract and conclusion, adds an explicit three-contribution list and acknowledgements, revises related work and limitations, and abbreviates positional-encoding terminology. It also corrects the query-reversion appendix reference. Most exposition and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Appendix prose changes from two-column to single-column layout, with extensive display relocation and an enlarged Figure 3. Table 5 is redesigned around four seen/unseen-query score columns, Table 2 gains RoPE rows, and new architecture and timing tables are inserted. The existing attention visualization is reused rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's untested encoder-only choice with architecture comparisons, adds a relevant RoPE comparator, and improves transparency through disaggregated embedding results, timing measurements, and explicit applicability limits. These provide a modest overall gain while preserving the core evidence. The additions remain imperfectly documented, particularly timing conditions, and broad best-performance statements require qualification given exceptions in Tables 2 and 15.
